record.title: Anthropic opens Claude Duet, a proactive work-agent preview
record.summary: Anthropic opened a US waitlist research preview of Claude Duet, a standalone and web-based assistant designed to monitor connected work accounts, initiate task updates and continue work in a hosted environment while the user is away. The company says Duet pauses for approval before consequential actions such as sending messages, paying, signing or deleting. The announcement describes more than 6,000 connectors and plugins. This records the announced product scope; independent evidence of reliability, adoption or productivity effects was not found.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Anthropic opened a waitlist research preview of Claude Duet on 2026-10-21 for US Pro and Max users. It is offered as a standalone iOS/Android app and on claude.ai, with the same plan usage limits as other Claude use.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Anthropic describes Duet as a proactive agent that checks connected accounts every few hours, continues tasks in a hosted virtual machine while the user is away, and requests approval before sending messages, making payments, signing documents or deleting items. The announcement lists more than 6,000 connectors and plugins.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Anthropic says the preview is early: Duet may misread messages or misjudge urgency, background checks consume plan limits, and the initial rollout is limited to US Pro and Max users by waitlist.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reliability or safety evaluation of Duet's connected-account monitoring, tool actions or approval gates was located.
No measured productivity, task success, intervention, error or economic outcomes were included in the launch announcement.

brief.importance_rationale: If the announced functions work as described, a persistent agent connected to business apps could move general assistants from request-response chat into recurring workflow execution. The score is bounded because access is a US waitlist preview and no independent performance, adoption or economic outcomes are reported.
limitations: The source is Anthropic's own product announcement and release notes; no independent inspection or adversarial evaluation of the product was performed.
The launch is a restricted waitlist preview, not general availability.
Anthropic says the early version can misread message threads or miscalibrate urgency; the announcement supplies no measured error rates or independent productivity results.
The announced approval gates and sensitive-information controls are not independently validated here.

technical.claimed_result: Anthropic announces a proactive work agent preview with periodic connected-account checks, background task execution and user approval before several consequential actions.
technical.demonstrated_result: The first-party announcement and release-note entry establish that Anthropic announced the preview and its stated access terms. Product performance and safeguard effectiveness were not independently demonstrated.
technical.mechanism: Anthropic says Duet uses a hosted virtual machine with its own browser to continue tasks in the background, checks connected accounts every few hours, and routes consequential actions through an explicit user-approval step. The announcement also describes credential protections and a classifier for sensitive information. These implementation details are vendor-reported and were not independently audited in this activation.
technical.regime: US Pro/Max users by waitlist; early research preview; checks every few hours; background usage draws on shared plan limits.
technical.strongest_baseline: No matched baseline or comparative productivity evaluation was reported in the announcement.

brief.title: Anthropic opens Claude Duet, a proactive work-agent preview
brief.why_it_matters: A persistent assistant that proactively checks work accounts and executes multi-step tasks could shift AI use from individual prompts toward recurring workflow delegation. Its practical importance depends on reliability, integration quality, cost and user oversight; the current evidence is a restricted vendor-run preview, not a measured productivity result.
